name: KickoffAPI — Football Data API (v1, legacy)
description:
Real-time football (soccer) data API: live scores, fixtures, results, deep player and team statistics, lineups, head-to-head, standings, transfers, in-play odds and 1,245 leagues in 171 countries, delivered as predictable JSON with rate-limit headers on every response. Authenticate by sending your key in the x-api-key header.

## v1 is legacy
v1 stays live until its sunset on 01 January 2027 and is frozen. New integrations should use v2, which has KickoffAPI's own string identifiers and a `{ data, meta }` envelope.

## Response format — flat by default, nested on request
Every `/api/v1` response is wrapped in `{ get, parameters, errors, results, paging, response }`. What is inside `response` is the question, and the answer is **the flat row by default**: `id`, `date`, `status`, `homeTeam`, `homeTeamId`, `goalsHome`, `elapsed` and the rest, all at the top level. That is the body every existing integration already parses and it does not change.

Ask for the nested `{ fixture, league, teams, goals, score }` form — which is what a client migrating from another football feed expects — in any of three ways:
* `?format=nested` on the request; * `?format=flat` to force the flat row back, from any client, whatever else is
  in the headers;


`GET /leagues` and `GET /fixtures` and `GET /fixtures/headtohead` are the three endpoints that carry the nested shape.

## Rate limits
Per-minute: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` (reset is the next minute boundary). Per plan, per day (UTC): `X-RateLimit-Daily-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Daily-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Daily-Reset`. Every 429 carries a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Plans: Free 100/day (30/min), Starter 7,500/day (120/min), Pro 75,000/day (300/min), Ultra 250,000/day (600/min), Enterprise on request.
